es: Analizar un texto de opinión breve identificando su tesis, su tono y dos recursos de cautela o persuasión, apoyándote en evidencias del texto.

teaching.en: My thesis is simple: our town needs more bike lanes.

teaching.en: Safe lanes may encourage more families to cycle to school.

teaching.en: Surely nobody wants children to cycle in heavy traffic?

teaching.en: In cities with bike lanes, accidents fell by a third, so such plans deserve support.

prompt.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la tesis del autor.

choices.text: The library should stay open until eight.

hint.es: La tesis suele aparecer al principio, tras I believe.

origin.text: Our library closes at five, just when most people finish work. I believe it should stay open until eight. Some people may say that this would cost too much. However, the library already pays for heating and lights, so a few more hours would add little. Students also need a quiet place to study after school, and many homes are too small or too noisy. Parents who work all day could finally take their children to choose a book. Surely a town that loves books should let its people read them? Last year, the city of Redford opened its library in the evening, and visits rose by a third. I am not saying that every problem will disappear. Even so, the evidence suggests that longer hours would help families, students and workers.

origin.text: Many schools now ask students to leave their phones in a locker during lunch. In my view, this is a mistake. It is true that phones can distract us in class. Nevertheless, lunch is our free time, and a rule like this treats teenagers like small children. A survey in one school found that students talked more when phones were allowed, which may suggest that the real problem is not the phone. Some teachers say that phones make the room quieter, but I wonder whether silence is really the goal of lunch. Perhaps a better plan would be quiet tables for people who want to read or rest. Surely that is fairer than a ban?

answer.text: I firmly believe that our city should close its centre streets to cars on Sundays. First, a car-free centre would be safer, especially for children and older people. It would also be quieter, so families could walk, talk and enjoy the shops. It is true that some drivers may find it inconvenient, and some shops could lose a few customers. To some extent, I understand that worry. However, it seems that more people would come on foot, and they would spend time and money in the centre. On the other hand, we could keep one street open for deliveries and for people who cannot walk far. In short, a car-free Sunday would make our centre safer, calmer and friendlier, and I believe the benefits outweigh the costs.
accepted: I firmly believe that our city should close its centre streets to cars on Sundays. First, a car-free centre would be safer, especially for children and older people. It would also be quieter, so families could walk, talk and enjoy the shops. It is true that some drivers may find it inconvenient, and some shops could lose a few customers. To some extent, I understand that worry. However, it seems that more people would come on foot, and they would spend time and money in the centre. On the other hand, we could keep one street open for deliveries and for people who cannot walk far. In short, a car-free Sunday would make our centre safer, calmer and friendlier, and I believe the benefits outweigh the costs.

My position is clear: the streets of the centre should be closed to traffic on Sundays. Admittedly, it may be difficult for people who live far away, and I agree that the plan needs good buses. Perhaps the city could add a free bus on those days. Even so, I am convinced that the change would help. Children could play, people could meet, and the air would probably be cleaner. Some say shops would suffer, but it seems that busy streets usually bring more customers. To sum up, a quiet Sunday centre would be a great gift to everyone, and I think it is worth a try.

prompt.es: Responde al mensaje con tacto y defiende tu postura con matiz.

answer.text: Hi Sam, thank you for your message. I think you are saying that the cleaning is not shared fairly, and I understand why you feel that way. It is true that I have been out a lot this month, and I admit that some weeks you have done more than your part. However, I firmly believe the problem is partly my work schedule, because I finish late on most days and I am often too tired to clean. To some extent, that may explain why the flat looks worse than before. I'm afraid I cannot clean every day, but I would like to find a fair solution. Could we agree to make a weekly calendar? I could take the kitchen on Saturdays, and you could choose another task. What do you think? Let's review the plan in two weeks. Thanks again for being honest with me.
accepted: Hi Sam, thank you for your message. I think you are saying that the cleaning is not shared fairly, and I understand why you feel that way. It is true that I have been out a lot this month, and I admit that some weeks you have done more than your part. However, I firmly believe the problem is partly my work schedule, because I finish late on most days and I am often too tired to clean. To some extent, that may explain why the flat looks worse than before. I'm afraid I cannot clean every day, but I would like to find a fair solution. Could we agree to make a weekly calendar? I could take the kitchen on Saturdays, and you could choose another task. What do you think? Let's review the plan in two weeks. Thanks again for being honest with me.

Hello Sam, thanks for telling me how you feel. Your message suggests that I am not doing enough, and I can see why you are upset. Admittedly, I have not cleaned much lately, and I am sorry about that. Still, my new job means that I work late most evenings, so perhaps the real problem is time, not effort. I'm not sure a strict rule would help, but a simple calendar might. What if we share the tasks by day and I take the bathroom and the kitchen at weekends? We could try it for a month and then check whether it works for both of us. I hope that sounds fair, and thank you for being patient with me.
